args.notes: Bursty spec: bursts of 8 requests 0 ns apart, Poisson 2 req/us, p99 latency <= 0.4 us. A single iterative CORDIC (12 iters, ~12 cycles @ 150 MHz = 80 ns) cannot drain an 8-deep burst before the next burst arrives (avg 0.5 us apart) — expect queue buildup and p99 violation. Prior campaigns: iterative family reached the front; pipelined/unrolled_k/pipelined_m never did on this device, but this spec's latency constraint may favor pipelined (1-cycle latency, throughput-limited) designs. Prior area-min winner: iterative dw=16, n_iter=12, truncation (267 LUTs+FFs, 10.5 acc bits). Selection rule: min luts_plus_ffs among feasible.

args.lesson: For bursty specs (bursts of 8, Poisson 2 req/us, p99 <= 0.4 us), pipelined_m wins: dw=15, n_iter=14, m=7 (855 LUTs+FFs est, 10.6 acc bits, 59.6 MSPS, simulated p99 0.233 us). L1 analytic p99 bound was optimistic (~0.17 vs simulated 0.233) but still passed. pipelined_m reached the front here, unlike prior campaigns. No L3/L4 measured rows; back_annotate no_measured_data, finalize directly.
